clinical_justification: The patient, Gopal Rao, a 49‑year‑old male, has a primary diagnosis of pneumonia (SNOMED CT 233604007) with onset on 2026‑04‑25. Community‑acquired pneumonia admission criteria state that inpatient care is medically necessary when the patient exhibits hypoxaemia (SpO₂ < 92%), haemodynamic instability, inability to take oral medication, or a high severity score, and when a chest X‑ray confirms pulmonary consolidation. Given the acute nature of pneumonia and the need for close monitoring and intravenous therapy, the treating physician has deemed hospital admission essential. Supporting investigations such as a chest X‑ray and clinical parameters are required to fully substantiate the medical necessity as per the guidelines.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.3 Contents of a Pre-Authorisation Request
citations.quote:
### 3.3 Contents of a Pre-Authorisation Request
Diagnosis with code, proposed treatment, estimated cost, expected length of stay, the treating doctor's statement of medical necessity, and supporting investigation reports.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
citations.quote:
## 3. Pre-Authorisation  
### 3.1 When Pre-Authorisation Is Required
Prior authorisation is mandatory for (a) every planned In-patient Hospitalisation and (b) any treatment with an estimated cost above ₹50,000.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 3. Pre-Authorisation > 3.2 Emergency Admissions
citations.quote:
### 3.2 Emergency Admissions
For emergency admissions, the pre-authorisation request must be submitted within 24 hours of admission; treatment shall not be denied solely because authorisation followed admission within this period.

citations.section: Community-acquired Pneumonia — Admission Criteria > Medical Necessity of Admission
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity of Admission
Admission is justified by hypoxaemia (SpO₂ < 92%), haemodynamic instability, inability to take oral medication, or a high severity score. A chest X-ray confirming consolidation is required.
